column1: # Seconds per suite on GitHub's 2-core Linux machine, read from the suite tables in the parts' logs (21 Nov, CI-SPEED-2,
# founder A253): the median of the PASS rows of 3 green merge-queue batch runs with 18 parts (44874048135, 44873814853,
# 44872846061; 21 Nov 05:51-06:44 UTC; 54 parts, 628 suites, 3 rows each but 3 suites with 1; no retries, no FAIL).
# Why: the 15 Nov file timed about 490 of the 628 suites a batch now runs; the other 135 (2727 s measured) counted 30 s
# each, so parts were dealt unevenly and ran 1097-1971 s (longest 1.33 x mean; part 1 held check_bk5_start_browser.cjs,
# 617 s, timed 397). The 135 are added at the end; a timed suite takes the new median only where it moved by more than
# 10 s and 20 % (23 did; the other 357 moved less and keep their row, so this diff stays small). Re-dealing those runs'
# own times with this file: longest part 1332 s of suites at 18 parts (was 1495; 1257 with every median), 988 s at 24
# (mean 942); each part also spends about 250 s outside its suites (checkout, set-up, browser).
# Of the 6 suites on run-suites.sh's hand-set QUARANTINE list, 5 keep their 15 Nov times (batches skip them, so they
# weigh 0 there and these times count only in the nightly full set); check_fo3st2_availability_browser.ts has none: 30 s.
# check_b78_section_names.ts: 1230 s is its measured hang, not its pass time (it passes in 0-5 s, but twice ran into the
# 1200 s suite limit + 30 s kill, runs 42243001915 and 42377102612; see QUARANTINE). Its nightly part is dealt that time,
# so the part still ends inside the job limit when it hangs. Set it back to its pass time (0) when it leaves the quarantine.
# run-suites.sh --shard balances the shards by these times (longest first); a suite missing here counts as 30 s; a
# quarantined suite weighs 0 only where it is skipped (PR and queue checks), its time in the nightly full set.
# Refresh the same way when many suites are new (earlier files: 15 Nov, 8 batches with 8 parts; 14 Nov, 7ca355ba7).
